newsitem.title: CHINA: China punishes banks for raising interest rates.
newsitem.headline: China punishes banks for raising interest rates.

text.p: The central bank has fined two local bank savings outlets a total of 200,000 yuan ($24,000) and sacked several officials for illegally raising interest rates rises to woo depositors, official media said on Tuesday.

Central bank officials at the Shangqiu branch in central Henan province uncovered two bank outlets that had secretly raised interest rates to attract deposits, the Financial Morning Post said on Tuesday.
One savings outlet belonged to the China Agricultual Bank, the newspaper said, but it did not identify the other. It did not give details of the interest rates they offered.
The central bank sets interest rates on deposits and prohibits commercial banks from adjusting them for their own gains.
The central bank officials fined each outlet 100,000 yuan, the newspaper said.
The central bank also sacked five bank officials, it said.

Raising interest rates illegally to boost bank savings in Shangqiu had increased since the start of 1997 and had aroused the concern of central bank officials, the newspaper said, but gave no further details.
